source.title: The Platonic Universe: Do Foundation Models See the Same Sky?
source.authors: UniverseTBD Trinidad Borrell; S. Dillmann; Kshitij Duraphe; Furkan Eris; Kartheik G. Iyer; Ashod Khederlarian; A. Kumar; G. Marraffini; Michael J. Smith; Shashwat Sourav; Rocco Di Tella; John F. Wu

record.file_problem: None apparent; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses a different measure and setting from language-model loss scaling, but tests whether downstream task performance of pretrained models increases with parameter count.
record.gate_note: The paper cites neural scaling laws as background, but does not measure held-out language-model cross-entropy, training tokens, compute, power-law fits, or compute-optimal allocations. Its own relevant results are downstream linear-probe scores versus model parameter count.
record.test_reason: The study measures downstream performance (linear-probe R² for redshift, stellar mass and sSFR from frozen embeddings) against parameter count across about 30 pretrained vision and vision-language checkpoints. That is a result on V6 in a new setting (frozen vision foundation models, astronomy regression), so T3 fits better than T2. It uses a basket of existing checkpoints, not controlled training runs. It reports rank correlations and an ANCOVA, not a fitted predictive law, and it never measures pretraining loss.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right but incomplete. The authors' main conclusion is support for the Aristotelian over the strict Platonic Representation Hypothesis: local (MKNN) but not global (CKA) alignment tracks physics performance, including across DESI spectra and HSC imagery. Secondary conclusions: physics probe performance scales with capacity, and general-purpose models match the astronomy-specific AstroPT. DINOv3 and PaliGemma show that total parameter count is insufficient to predict convergence, and PaliGemma's larger language trunks do not improve recovery.
record.recipe_differences: Instead of scaling language-model training runs and measuring held-out cross-entropy, the study evaluates frozen pretrained vision and multimodal model embeddings using downstream linear probes of astronomical properties.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported capacity trend is not uniform across model families; PaliGemma 2's fixed-size SigLIP vision encoder and larger Gemma language trunk are associated with weaker physical-property recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: Representational alignment (permutation-calibrated MKNN, not CKA) rises with scale and with probe performance within families, across modalities and across architectures; DINOv3 students instead align more with their teacher as they grow.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Local representational convergence between models increases with model scale/performance.

record.problems: The outcomes are astronomical linear-probe scores, not language-model pretraining loss. The study tests a basket of pretrained checkpoints rather than controlled training runs or compute budgets; its capacity association does not establish a power law or extrapolation rule.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4 reports per-checkpoint probe scores for many additional models and targets. Those checkpoint-level results are not all transcribed here; the aggregate scaling results, per-property correlations, and all six reported PaliGemma 3B-to-28B declines are retained.

untested.parts: Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss; any fitted functional form or extrapolation of downstream performance; language tasks; language-only models.
Not tested: no pretraining loss measured.
Not tested: no pretraining-loss power law in vision.

missing.what: ANCOVA R² ~ log Nparams + C(family) giving a positive capacity coefficient (HSC p=0.002, JWST p=2e-5): the within-family scaling test.
Within-family non-monotonic cases besides PaliGemma 28B: PaliGemma 10B ≈ 3B; DINOv3 vitl16/vith16plus below vitb16 on HSC; I-JEPA Giant ≈ Huge; CLIP Large ≈ Base on HSC; LLaVA 13B ≈ 7B.
Layerwise PaliGemma probing showing physics recovery declines through the Gemma trunk.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche changed from T2 to T3 (new setting: frozen vision/VLM embeddings, astronomy regression). The evidence for V6 is correlational across heterogeneous public checkpoints, so 'predictably' rests on rank correlations, not a fitted law. Width-group ANOVA (p=0.46, 0.31) argues the trend is not probe capacity. The paper's dates (ICLR 2027, v2 Sep 2026) are as stated in the text.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out language-model pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Extrapolating loss from smaller runs to much larger runs.
Compute-optimal parameter/token allocations and their trends with compute.
Whether architecture details such as depth and width have only small effects at fixed parameter count.
Whether power-law pretraining-loss forms hold in other modalities or training regimes.
The study tests downstream physical-property prediction from frozen embeddings against parameter count; it does not test downstream performance against pretraining loss or on language tasks.
Dependence of loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on fitting choices, and departures from power-law loss curves.

relationships.condition: Across the basket of frozen vision/VLM checkpoints, HSC and JWST imagery, all three probe targets
relationships.reason: Significant positive rank correlations of probe R² with parameter count, ρ≈0.43–0.67 (r1–r8). Per the text, the capacity effect survives a within-family ANCOVA. The association is moderate and no law is fitted.
relationships.display_finding: Probe R² had significant positive rank correlations of approximately 0.43–0.67 with parameter size, and the capacity association persisted after within-family adjustment.

relationships.condition: PaliGemma 2 family, where scale is added only to the language trunk with a fixed SigLIP vision encoder
relationships.reason: The 28B checkpoint scores below the 3B on all six target×modality probes (r9–r14). The authors attribute this to where capacity is added, so parameter count alone does not predict downstream gains.
relationships.display_finding: The 28B checkpoint scored below 3B on all six target-by-modality probes while the vision encoder remained fixed.
